correctness.rationale: The source proves \(d(C^\perp)=4\) and that distinct minimum dual supports form a \(3\)-\((q+1,4,\lambda)\) design with \(\lambda=p^\ell-2\). A size-three recovery set for coordinate \(i\) yields a dual check supported in its union with \(i\); dual distance \(4\) forces equality with a minimum dual support. Conversely every minimum dual support gives a three-helper parity recovery. Two independent dual words cannot share a weight-four support, since cancellation at one coordinate would create dual weight at most three. Derivation at \(i\) therefore gives the exact simple \(2\)-\((q,3,\lambda)\) repair design. Standard design counting yields the block, degree, and pair-codegree formulas, and inclusion-exclusion followed by greedy matching gives the stated availability lower bound. An exhaustive \(\mathbb F_{81}\) reconstruction independently verifies the \(q=9\) instance.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly presents the code as a distributed-storage LRC application, so the multiplicity and disjointness of its repair groups are intrinsic operational invariants. The result upgrades locality from existence of one three-helper repair to a complete balanced repair topology, giving exact per-coordinate repair counts and a uniform availability guarantee that grows with \(q\). This is a structural consequence of the new 3-design family rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
